decisions.reason: As an adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display, it remains very close to the firm's core retail-display capabilities and is still useful for customer-specific problem solving despite the lack of recent website visibility.
The pegboard-back cardboard display is a differentiated but still standard in-store format that fits the firm's focused paper-based display portfolio and service model well.
This generic cardboard quarter-pallet display overlaps strongly with other core formats, and with no recent visibility it is the most logical candidate for portfolio rationalisation.
The media-oriented quarter-pallet display is more niche and less future-proof than the firm's broader core display offer, so resources are better shifted to established business and new development.
